findings.title: Get root on a musl Linux system by slamming it with an overly long password
findings.summary_md: The Register reports that researcher Özgün Kültekin discovered the *sshole authentication bypass, tracked as CVE-2026-123158, in OpenSSH on musl-based Linux systems such as Alpine. An attacker who can reach the SSH port can log into accounts configured to reject passwords using any password longer than 256 characters. The report was published on November 5, 2026.

findings.title: sshole (CVE-2026-123158): OpenSSH password bypass on Alpine Linux
findings.summary_md: On November 5, 2026, OpenSSH released version 10.6p2 and Alpine Linux published fixed openssh packages for the password authentication bypass tracked as CVE-2026-123158. The bug affects OpenSSH built against the musl C library without PAM. An attacker who can reach the SSH port can log into an account that has no password by sending a very long password.

findings.title: OpenSSH Password Authentication Bypass on Alpine Linux (*sshole) – CVE-2026-123158
findings.summary_md: OpenSSH released version 10.6p2 on November 5, 2026 to address a password authentication bypass affecting Linux systems that use musl libc without PAM, including Alpine Linux. OX Security's review of the research at sshhole.com found the flaw was located by building sshd across glibc, musl, PAM and no-PAM combinations and running roughly 17,600 deliberate tests. Alpine released fixes the same day.
